advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) because its methods operate on two distinct sets of attributes: formatting/display logic (`_width`, `title`, `describe_customer`) and data retrieval/communication logic (`_repository`, `_mailer`, `order_count`, `mail_summary`). Additionally, the class violates architectural layering by directly importing infrastructure components (`OrderRepository`, `EmailClient`) from the presentation layer, and it displays feature envy towards the `customer` object in `describe_customer`.

suggestions.title: Extract formatting logic into a dedicated Presentation Formatter
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class `ReportFormatter` in the presentation layer that holds `_width` and contains `title()` and `describe_customer()`. `ReportView` should delegate these calls to an instance of `ReportFormatter`. This separates the 'how to display' concern from the 'what data to fetch' concern.

suggestions.title: Introduce Application Service to mediate Infrastructure access
suggestions.sketch: Create an `OrderReportService` in the application layer that depends on `OrderRepository` and `EmailClient`. This service exposes high-level methods like `get_order_count()` and `send_summary(address)`. `ReportView` (presentation) will now depend only on this application service, removing direct imports of infrastructure classes and resolving the layer violation.
notes: addresses_smells names labels the target does not carry: layer_violation

advices.risk_notes: Refactoring to an application service increases the number of classes and may slightly increase overall system complexity (NOM across the system). The `describe_customer` method currently accesses `customer` attributes directly; moving this to a formatter is safe, but ensure the `customer` object passed is the correct domain type. The architectural fix requires updating the dependency injection container or factory to wire the new application service.
